Snapline 2.2.0

  • Smart Redact sees faces and people — two new opt-in detectors in the Smart Redact settings find human faces and full or partial figures: bystanders, video-call tiles, profile photos. Each detection becomes an ordinary redaction — blur, pixelate, or solid, individually deletable — in the editor’s scan and the after-capture pass alike.
  • One subject, one annotation: a face inside a detected person is covered by the person box alone, so deleting a false positive never leaves an orphaned box behind. In Tall Captures, a figure crossing a scan seam comes back as a single box, not two halves.
  • The completion message counts per detector (“Found 3 faces and 1 person”), a clean scan says so explicitly, and if one detector can’t read an image the others’ results still land — with a note naming what didn’t run. All detection is on-device; nothing leaves your Mac, and no new permissions are needed.

Snapline 2.1.0

  • Backgrounds — the annotation editor gains a Background stage: wrap a capture in a gradient or solid-color backdrop with padding, rounded corners, and a drop shadow before sharing. Ten gradient presets or any solid color; the result is baked into Copy, Done, Save to File, and drag-out alike.
  • Background settings stay editable. Reopen a capture from History and the backdrop, padding, corners, and shadow are yours to change — the original pixels are untouched underneath.
  • Snapline remembers your last Background configuration and offers it on the next capture you annotate. Off by default; Tall Captures are excluded.

Snapline 2.0.4

  • Settings, History, the annotation editor, the trim editor and the text view now appear in ⌘-Tab and the Dock while they are open, so you can switch back to a window after moving to another app. They were previously unreachable once Snapline was no longer frontmost.
  • A Window menu lists every open Snapline window, as a second way back to one.
